A_gt_provenance.note: Reference = experimental-PDB DSSP (p['ss8'], p['pctH']) from RCSB X-ray; loaded from proteins.json, not generated by either predictor.

B_normalization.note: Predicted %H normalized by sequence length (protein-level percentage); no division by a model-derived max/mean. mean_%H descriptive only, not used in Pearson r.

C_result_existence.note: All cited values present exactly in on-disk result.json. V1: Q3=0.6579, r=0.8505, p=3.84e-57, frameRec=1.0. V2: Q3=0.8592, r=0.9792, p=1.88e-215, frameRec=1.0. Computed in main() invoked under __main__.

D_dead_code.note: Scoring loops, Pearson calls, frame-recovery loops, result writes all on executed main() paths; no uncalled evaluation.

E_scope.note: Evidence supports the claim on two finite sets (200 heldout / 310 fresh); one run per variant; frame recovery on <=100 proteins. Keep wording limited to tested conditions; do not generalize to arbitrary proteins/seeds.

F_eval_type.note: Central SS->%H correlation uses real experimental-DSSP GT. Frame-recovery subtest uses synthetic reverse-translation/ORF (method-independent proxy) but does not make the DSSP correlation model-derived.

key_findings: Both variants use experimental-DSSP labels, not evaluated-model predictions.
Reported Q3/r/p/frame-recovery exactly match on-disk result files and are on live execution paths.
No self-referential normalization or dead evaluation code.
Scope limited to tested held-out/fresh sets; frame recovery on synthetic reverse-translated subset.
rationale: Methodology substantially trustworthy: experimentally-derived GT, non-self-normalized correlation, cited outputs present and connected to executed code. Only limitation is scope (one run per variant, finite sets) -> WARN, not FAIL.
